mode.label: Pear
mode.note: 110.0 kg; a pear-shaped body with narrow sloping shoulders over huge hips and thighs, stubby legs, short arms and a small head, walking slowly at 0.8 m/s. Its stride is held to a side-to-side waddle: the trunk rocking 3–6°, feet 22–32 cm apart, the pelvis rolling 2–6°, and the short arms held out over the hips, barely swinging (4–10°); the search finds the cheapest walk in that style. Simulated with a simpler pipeline than the other bodies (a searched stride, inverse dynamics and static optimization; see How it works). Bipedal walk; the best bipedal run found costs 7% less and the best two-footed hop found costs 0% less, though this model is less faithful for gaits with a flight phase.

lede: A muscle-driven 3D animal walks on the gait that minimizes its metabolic cost, with its bones kept apart and its head held steady and level. Switch between fourteen bodies: the quadruped, the same body with long forelimbs and broad shoulders, that body with ten legs, a three-legged walker, a six-legged one, four humanoids (a test biped, a thin kid, a lumbering ogre and a lanky giant) and five comic bipeds (a bobblehead, a hooded hunchback, a beanpole, a pear-shaped waddler and a top-heavy brute); everything below follows the selected body. All walk at 1 m/s except the ogre at 0.7 m/s, the hood at 0.6 m/s and the pear at 0.8 m/s.
compareSub: The pear (110.0 kg, 1.70 m, at 0.8 m/s) is the biped reshaped: narrow sloping shoulders over huge hips and thighs, stubby legs, short arms and a small head.
